newsitem.title: INDONESIA: S.E.Asian Cocoa - Prices lower, supply seen mixed.
newsitem.headline: S.E.Asian Cocoa - Prices lower, supply seen mixed.

text.p: Southeast Asian cocoa prices were weaker on Wednesday, with the market moving sideways in Indonesia while demand was steady in Malaysia, traders said.
Indonesian traders said the main crop harvest was proceeding well, with supply remaining ample. But they said prices were weaker in line with declines in New York futures.
"The market is relatively quiet at this moment," one trader said. "Prices are drifting, and buying activity is not very strong because of overseas' factors."

Traders said fair average quality (FAQ) cocoa beans were quoted at 2,975-3,000 rupiah/kg in Ujung Pandang, capital of the key growing region of South Sulawesi, compared with 3,040-3,050 rupiah/kg a week ago.
Cocoa was quoted at 3,486 rupiah/kg in the North Sumatran capital of Medan, compared with 3,512 rupiah last week.
"Demand is rather flat at this moment," one Medan trader said. "We are expecting some bids from exporters soon."
The traders said grinders were relying heavily on beans imported from Indonesia and other producing countries.
They said prices were fundamentally supported by a bad early crop for 1997, which was expected to slash Malaysia's usual mid-year cocoa harvest by 60 percent.

On Wednesday, the Malaysian Cocoa Board quoted Standard Malaysian Cocoa (SMC) Grade 1 A out of Tawau at an average of 3,425 ringgit a tonne and Grade 1B, also out of Tawau, at an average of 3,375 ringgit.
Compared to Tuesday, both grades were up eight ringgit.

Traders said the market was waiting for price direction from New York, where the July contract closed unchanged at $1,449 a tonne on Tuesday. Second-month September rose $3 to $1,488 while the back months sagged $1.
"Supply is Ujung Pandang seems ample at the moment, with the harvest proceeding well," one trader said. "Some players are covering positions, but there's not much activity."
Malaysian traders said the market was fundamentally strong and did not reflect the mixed prices in New York overnight.
"The demand is still very much there, only there's not enough (cocoa beans) to go around," a cocoa mill owner said.
But if compared to a week ago, the 1 A was down three ringgit, while the B 1 fell 13 ringgit.
On Wednesday, trading houses quoted the 1A at around 3,475 and the 1 B at 3,395-3,405.
